text:
Among the statements (I – IV), the correct ones
are:

(I) Be has smaller atomic radius compared to
Mg.

(II) Be has higher ionization enthalpy than Al.

(III) Charge/radius ratio of Be is greater than
that of Al.

(IV) Both Be and Al form mainly covalent
compounds.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(I) Atomic radius increases down a group, so Be is smaller than Mg; true.

(II) The first ionization enthalpy of Be ($899\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is higher than that of Al ($577\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$); true.

(III) The diagonal relationship between Be and Al arises because $\mathrm{Be}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$ have nearly the same charge/radius ratio, so the claim that the ratio for Be is greater is not correct.

(IV) The small, highly polarising $\mathrm{Be}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$ ions make both elements form mainly covalent compounds, such as $\mathrm{BeCl}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{AlCl}{}_{3}$; true.

The correct statements are (I), (II) and (IV).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Consider the hypothetical situation where the
azimuthal quantum number,
$l$, takes values 0,
1, 2, ....., n + 1, where n is the principal
quantum number. Then, the element with
atomic number :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $l=0,1,\ldots ,n+1$, the shell $n=1$ has $1s$, $1p$ and $1d$ subshells (capacities 2, 6, 10), and $n=2$ has $2s$, $2p$, $2d$ and $2f$.

Filling each shell completely before the next, in order of increasing $n$ and then $l$, gives the sequence $1s,1p,1d,2s,2p,\ldots$

$Z=13$: $1s^{2}1p^{6}1d^{5}$; the valence $1d$ subshell is half-filled, so (A) is true.

$Z=9$ ($1s^{2}1p^{6}1d^{1}$) is not an alkali metal, $Z=8$ ($1s^{2}1p^{6}$) does not complete the $n=1$ shell, so it is not a noble gas, and $Z=6$ ($1s^{2}1p^{4}$) has a $1p$, not a $2p$, valence subshell.

Filling by the $(n+l)$ rule would place $2s$ before $1d$ and make both (B) and (C) true, so only the shell-by-shell order gives a single correct option.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
The decreasing order of reactivity of the
following compounds towards nucleophilic
substitution $(S_{N}2)$ is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$ substitution at the benzylic $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$ carbon, electron-withdrawing groups on the ring increase the partial positive charge on that carbon and stabilise the transition state, so reactivity rises with the total electron withdrawal by the ring substituents.

(I) has no substituent and is the least reactive. In (IV) both $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ groups are meta and withdraw only by the $-I$ effect.

In (III) the para $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ withdraws by both the $-M$ and $-I$ effects and the meta $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ by $-I$, so (III) is more reactive than (IV).

In (II) the ortho $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ withdraws by $-M$ and by the strongest $-I$ effect, being nearest to the benzylic carbon, and the meta $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ adds a further $-I$ effect, so (II) is the most reactive.

$\text{(II)}>\text{(III)}>\text{(IV)}>\text{(I)}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
The increasing order of the reactivity of the
following compounds in nucleophilic addition
reaction is :

Propanal, Benzaldehyde, Propanone, Butanone
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition increases with the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and decreases with crowding around it.

Ketones carry two electron-releasing alkyl groups on the carbonyl carbon and are less reactive than aldehydes; butanone, with the larger ethyl group, is less reactive than propanone.

In benzaldehyde, conjugation of the carbonyl group with the benzene ring lowers the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon, so it is less reactive than propanal, but with only one substituent it remains more reactive than the two ketones.

Increasing order: butanone < propanone < benzaldehyde < propanal.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text: The incorrect statement is :
options:
In manganate and permanganate ions, the π-bonding takes place by overlap of p-orbitals
of oxygen and d-orbitals of manganese

Manganate ion is green in colour and
permanganate ion is purple in colour

Manganate and permanganate ions are
paramagnetic

Manganate and permanganate ions are
tetrahedral
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To identify the incorrect statement, let's analyze each option :

Option A : "In manganate and permanganate ions, the π-bonding takes place by overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen and d-orbitals of manganese." 
This statement is true. In both manganate $MnO_{4}^{2-}$ and permanganate $MnO_{4}^{-}$ ions, the manganese atom is in a high oxidation state (+6 and +7, respectively) and forms bonds with oxygen atoms involving the overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen and d-orbitals of manganese.

Option B : "Manganate ion is green in colour and permanganate ion is purple in colour."
This statement is true. Manganate ions are indeed green and permanganate ions are purple in aqueous solution.

Option C : "Manganate and permanganate ions are paramagnetic."
This statement is incorrect. Manganate ion (Mn in +6 state, $3d^{1})$ is paramagnetic, but permanganate ion (Mn in +7 state, $3d^{0})$ has no unpaired electron and is diamagnetic.

Manganate($Mn^{+6}O_{4}$
$^{2–})$
,

Mn(25) = [Ar]$3d^{5}4s^{2}$

$Mn^{+6}(25) =$ [Ar]$3d^{1}$ $\to$ Paramagnetic

Permanganate ($Mn^{+7}O_{4}^{-})$

Mn(25) = [Ar]$3d^{5}4s^{2}$

$Mn^{+7}(25) =$ [Ar]$3d^{0}$ $\to$ Diamagnetic
Option D : "Manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral."
This statement is true. Both manganate and permanganate ions have a tetrahedral geometry, with the manganese atom at the center and the four oxygen atoms surrounding it.

Therefore, the incorrect statement is option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
C undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. KOH to give potassium benzoate and benzyl alcohol, so C is benzaldehyde, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}$. D undergoes aldol condensation with $\mathrm{Ba}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}$ to give mesityl oxide, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, so D is acetone.

Reductive ozonolysis of B gives $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}$ and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, so B, the product of the first step, is $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ (2-methyl-1-phenylprop-1-ene).

With A = $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by water gives the tertiary alcohol $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, and conc. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ removes water to give the alkene conjugated with the benzene ring, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$.

The ketones in options A, B and C give alkenes of the type $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=$, whose ozonolysis gives acetophenone, which cannot undergo the Cannizzaro reaction.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Consider the following molecules and
statements related to them :

[IMG]


(a) (B) is more likely to be crystalline than (A)

(b) (B) has higher boiling point than (A)

(c) (B) dissolves more readily than (A) in water

Identify the correct option from below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) is salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Its adjacent $-\mathrm{OH}$ and $-\mathrm{COOH}$ groups form an intramolecular hydrogen bond ($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\cdot \cdot \cdot \mathrm{O}=\mathrm{C}$), so each molecule stays largely self-contained.

(B) is 4-hydroxybenzoic acid. Its $-\mathrm{OH}$ and $-\mathrm{COOH}$ groups are too far apart to bond to each other, so they form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with neighbouring molecules, building an extended network.

(a) True: the intermolecular network holds molecules of (B) in a regular, tightly packed lattice, so (B) crystallises more readily (m.p. of (B) about $214{}^{\circ }\text{C}$ against about $159{}^{\circ }\text{C}$ for (A)).

(b) True: stronger intermolecular attraction in (B) needs more energy to overcome, so (B) boils at a higher temperature.

(c) True: the free $-\mathrm{OH}$ and $-\mathrm{COOH}$ groups of (B) hydrogen-bond with water, whereas in (A) they are partly engaged with each other, so (B) dissolves more readily.

The hydrogen bond in (A) is intramolecular and does not link molecules together, so it lowers rather than raises crystallinity and boiling point.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Complex A has a composition of $H_{12}O_{6}Cl_{3}Cr$. If the complex on treatment with conc.$H_{2}SO_{4}$
 loses
13.5% of its original mass, the correct molecular formula of A is :

[Given: atomic mass of Cr = 52 amu and Cl = 35 amu]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The formula $\mathrm{H}{}_{12}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}\mathrm{Cr}$ corresponds to $\mathrm{CrCl}{}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, with molar mass

$M=6(18)+3(35)+52=265\text{g mol}^{-1}$

Concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ is a dehydrating agent: it removes only water of crystallisation held outside the coordination sphere, not water bonded to Cr and not chloride.

Mass lost per mole $=0.135\times 265=35.8\text{g}\approx 2\times 18\text{g}$, so A contains 2 molecules of lattice water.

The other 4 $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ are coordinated to Cr; with coordination number 6, two $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ complete the coordination sphere and the third $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is the counter ion, giving $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]\mathrm{Cl}\cdot 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
An acidic solution of dichromate is electrolyzed
for 8 minutes using 2A current. As per the
following equation

$Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-}$
 $+ 14H^{+} + 6e^{–}$ $\to$ $2Cr^{3+} + 7H_{2}O$

The amount of $Cr^{3+}$ obtained was 0.104 g. The
efficiency of the process(in%) is
(Take : F = 96000 C, At. mass of chromium = 52)
$______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Charge passed: $Q=It=2\times 8\times 60=960\text{C}$, i.e. $\dfrac{960}{96000}=0.01$ mol of electrons.

In $\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}{}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+6\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}+7\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, 6 mol of electrons give 2 mol of $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$, i.e. 3 mol of electrons per mol of $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ (Cr goes from +6 to +3).

Theoretical mass of $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$:

$m=\dfrac{0.01}{3}\times 52=0.1733\text{g}$

$\text{Efficiency}=\dfrac{0.104}{0.1733}\times 100=60%$

Hence, the answer is 60.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
If $250 cm^{3}$
 of an aqueous solution containing 0.73 g of a protein A is isotonic with one litre of
another aqueous solution containing 1.65 g of a protein B, at 298 K, the ratio of the molecular
masses of A and B is $______ × 10^{–2} ($to the nearest integer).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let molar mass of protein A = x g/mol

Let molar mass of protein B = y g/mol

$π_{A}$ = osmotic pressure of protein A = $\frac{0.73}{x}\times \frac{1000}{250}\times RT$

$π_{B}$ = osmotic pressure of protein B = $\frac{1.65}{y}\times \frac{1}{1}\times RT$

Given $π_{A}$ = $π_{B}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{0.73}{x}\times \frac{1000}{250}\times RT$ = $\frac{1.65}{y}\times \frac{1}{1}\times RT$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x}{y}$ = $\frac{0.73}{0.25\times 1.65}$ = 1.77

= 177 $\times$ $10^{-2}$
